results.ev: Two jacket FRONTS (upper chest/lapel area only), captioned "Both sides" and "Each side o...". This is a lapel-buttonhole POSITION diagram. No sleeve, no cuff, no buttonhole stitching shown, and nothing expresses hand-vs-machine.
Same lapel-buttonhole position chart, off-register crop; the fully visible jacket front is captioned "Right". No sleeve or cuff appears; machine stitching is never depicted.

Trouser FRONT view (J-curve fly topstitch at centre front, slanted on-seam side pockets, belt loops). Four red dart marks (two per side) sit below the FRONT waistband, i.e. front darts as an alternative to pleats. Filename reads "No_pleat_double_darts" and data-store/image-rejections.json records the source as factory/kute/trousers/Style_Pleat_style_Pleat_style/302Y__No_pleat_double_darts.jpeg - the vendor's PLEAT STYLE chart. The catalog option describes back darts creating "pronounced seat curvature"; the seat/back panel is never shown.

Trouser FRONT view (fly J-curve, front slant pockets, belt loops), no red dart marks anywhere. It is the "no pleat, no dart" FRONT drawing - the same file is used in trousers.json as the techpackIllustration for pleat-style option "Flat Front (No Dart)" (line 1317). The option's own text says "Flat back panel", but no back panel or seat is depicted.

Trouser FRONT view with two red dart marks (one per side) below the FRONT waistband, either side of the fly. Filename "No_pleat_single_dart"; image-rejections.json records the source folder as Style_Pleat_style_Pleat_style (front pleat/dart chart) and already lists key "trousers|back-darts|darts-single" as rejected for the builder role. Dart count is shown, but on the wrong panel - no back view, seat or back pockets.

Not a garment drawing at all - a BUTTON product sheet. Photographed 4-hole buttons with captions "N304/FK3132BK  HORN BUTTON" and "NJ0...", plus Japanese header text "...配置" and "...ning". Nothing about a chest dart or a +2 cm extension.
Another crop of the same BUTTON sheet: photographed buttons captioned "G515/FK283214  COROZO BUTTON" and "...06/FKE03237". No jacket, no dart, no measurement.
A single photographed metal/horn button captioned "BK219/FK763274" on white. No jacket hem, no front edge, no curve.
A single photographed button captioned "SZ215/FK763236" (engraved ring visible on the button face). Button sheet crop, not a hem shape.
A single photographed button captioned "BK223/FK763231", with "CUSTOM" lettering engraved around the button rim. Button sheet crop, not a squared jacket hem.

Crop of an exterior POCKET STYLE chart: tiles captioned "Regular Slanted Flap in 4.5cm" and "Regular Slanted Flap in 5cm" with blue dimension callouts "4.5cm" / "5cm". The field is "Interior Columbia Stitching / Piping" - no interior, lining seam, taping or piping is shown.

Same pocket-style chart, different crop: captions "...Jetted Flap in 5cm", "Straight Jetted Pocket", "Straight Welt P..." with callouts "1.2cm", "1.5cm", "1cm". Depicts hip-pocket variants, not interior Columbia stitching.

Pocket-style chart crop: a checkmarked tile captioned "Straight Jetted Flap in 4.5cm" (callout "4.5cm"), plus "Angled Box Pleat Patch Pocket" and a partial third tile with "1.2cm". Used for TWO options: columbia-piping "None" (should show absence of interior stitching/piping - shows exterior pockets instead) and chest-pocket "None" (should show a jacket with no chest pocket - the drawing plainly shows pockets present, and they are hip/patch pockets, not a breast pocket).

Same pocket chart again: captions "...Pocket in 1.2cm", "Straight Welt Pocket in 1.5cm", "Regular Slanted Flap in ..." with callouts "1.5cm", "4cm", "1cm". Shows welt/flap pocket geometry, not interior piping trim.

Crop of a LAPEL STYLE chart - six lapel line drawings captioned "8C Notch Lapel", "8L Peak Lapel", "10° Peak Lapel", "Notch lapel 2", "Notch lapel 4", "Notch lapel 6", with red Japanese annotations giving hook/spacing measurements ("...14cm", "...12cm"). The field is external decoration (siblings are front-chest horizontal/slanted button loops); no decoration or its absence is expressed.

Crop of the edge/top-stitch chart. The fully visible jacket front is captioned "Top Stitch 4CM to edge"; the half-cropped one reads "...itching". That chart's discriminator is stitch distance from the edge, not which areas receive hand stitching. Shoulder seam, vents, chest pocket edges and buttonholes are not called out anywhere, and the back/vents are never shown.

Off-register crop of the same edge-stitch chart. The half-cut jacket at the left edge is captioned "...lone" (i.e. "None"), which does correspond to the label, but the dominant, fully visible jacket is a competing variant captioned "0.15cm edge by ma[chine]" with a blue "0.15cm" callout. Right subject family (a clean jacket front with no decorative lines) but the frame advertises another option, and at 240x200 no stitch line is legible either way.

Edge-stitch chart crop: the checkmarked (blue-bordered) tile is captioned "...y machine" (0.15cm edge by machine) and the right tile "0.15cm edge by hand", both with "0.15cm" callouts pointing at the FRONT edge/lapel. Front views only - no shoulder seam detail and no stitching at the shoulder.

Crop of a LAPEL WIDTH chart - jacket FRONT/chest close-ups captioned "...7cm" and "7.5cm" with a red 7.5cm measuring line drawn across the lapel. A back-vent option needs a rear view; there is no back, no vent, and no belt.

Same lapel-width chart, adjacent crop: front views captioned "8cm" and "8.5cm" with red lapel measuring lines, and a stray UI "Search" box captured at the top right (screenshot artefact). No rear view, vent or belt.

Crop of a button/buttonhole diagram: a blue-bordered selection tile that is ~70% empty white, with two round 4-hole buttons at the right edge, each with a pink/red horizontal BUTTONHOLE slit drawn beside it (siblings i-bartack.jpg and x-bartack.jpg are crops of the same button column). No inner breast pocket, no pocket corner, and no D-shaped bartack stitch anywhere.

Crop shows two round 4-hole buttons stacked vertically at the left edge beside a double vertical garment edge line - a sleeve/cuff button column. There is no inner pocket, no welt or pocket mouth, and no bartack stitch bar anywhere in frame. Decisive: its sibling x-bartack.jpg is the same button column mirrored, so the pair differs by SIDE, not by I-shaped vs X-shaped bartack. The field's discriminator is entirely absent.

Essentially blank. The whole 240x200 canvas is paper-white except one thin vertical line down the left side. No pocket, no interior facing, no garment feature at all - nothing that could depict an open (unclosed) inner pocket.

Shows two 4-hole buttons with pink/red horizontal keyhole BUTTONHOLES drawn to the left of each, against a vertical garment edge line - a cuff/placket button-and-buttonhole diagram. No X-shaped bartack, no pocket mouth, no pocket at all. Mirror image of i-bartack.jpg.

Pure text, no drawing whatsoever. The crop is a column of Chinese hand-sewing operations: 手工封胸袋/ 手工捉袖山头里/ 手工捉袖口里/ 手工捉下摆里/ 手工捉后叉里/ 手工内珠边/ 手工套结封下口袋/ 手工捉里子肩缝/ 手工捉领底呢 (hand-close chest pocket / hand-stitch sleeve-head lining / hand-stitch cuff lining / hand-stitch hem lining / hand-stitch back-vent lining / hand inner pick-stitch edge / hand bartack closing lower pocket / hand-stitch lining shoulder seam / hand-stitch undercollar felt). This is a hand-work specification list, not a ticket pocket illustration.

A text fragment cut mid-character. Shows a lone black glyph 工 and a red partial …准) - the tail of (以选项为准) meaning 'subject to the selected option' - against a navy table border. No garment, no pocket, no drawing.

Crop of a table heading, cut mid-word: black 部位手… ('part / hand-work…') above red (以选项为… ('subject to the selected…'), with the navy cell border on the left. Text only - no garment and no pocket, and nothing expressing left vs right.

Jacket-interior line drawing captioned in English 'Diamond shape left pocket', with the neighbouring grid cell's caption 'RIGHT JET[TED]' cut off at the right edge. These are the PEN-POCKET option captions, so this is a crop of the pen-pocket option grid, a different field entirely - it does not depict an MP3/media pocket.

Captioned 'Left jetted pocket' inside a navy selected-state box with a large blue checkmark, alongside the neighbouring caption 'Drop shape left p[ocket]'. Wrong on two counts: it is the pen-pocket option grid rather than the MP3 pocket, and it shows a pocket PRESENT and actively selected while the label is 'None'.

Jacket interior captioned 'Drop shape right pen pocket', with the neighbouring cell reading 'Diamo[nd]'. The caption explicitly names the PEN pocket, not an MP3 pocket - a crop of the wrong option grid.

Crop of the neck/shoulder corner of a jacket front panel, with a red dashed stitch line running along the SHOULDER SEAM. No pocket, no interior facing, and only one side of the garment is in frame - so it cannot express 'both sides' either.

The same neckline/shoulder-corner pattern piece as both.jpg but mirrored, again with red dashed stitching along the shoulder seam, plus stray sleeve-button and thread marks clipped at the bottom edge. A shoulder-seam construction detail, not a namecard pocket.

Two unrelated fragments side by side: a collar/undercollar pattern piece with red hatch marks, and a sleeve-cuff corner showing a column of 4 stacked buttons against a red dash-dot vent line. A cuff-button diagram - no jacket interior and no pocket.
A sleeve-cuff/vent corner with 4 stacked black buttons and a red 'X' mark beneath them. This is a sleeve button diagram; there is no interior facing and no namecard pocket anywhere in frame.
Essentially blank - white canvas with a single diagonal line near the right edge and nothing else. No pocket, no diamond-shaped welt, no identifiable garment part.

Upper-body crop showing the back neckline/collar band (double horizontal line with the centre-back seam dropping from it) and the collar-to-lapel NOTCH highlighted in red, with the lapel edge running down to the lower right. This is a gorge/notch geometry diagram, not a pen pocket, and there is no drop-shaped welt anywhere.
The same collar-to-lapel notch highlighted in red as left-drop.jpg, mirrored to the opposite side of the frame. No jetted pocket, no welt lips, no pocket mouth - lapel/gorge geometry only.

Again the collar band with centre-back seam plus the red-highlighted collar-to-lapel notch, with a stray diagonal line at the right of frame. Gorge/notch geometry; no diamond pocket and no pocket of any kind.
Red-highlighted collar/lapel notch positioned at the right of frame, with two heavy diagonal lines at the far left. Lapel gorge detail - no pocket of any shape is drawn.
Essentially blank - white canvas with only two diagonal lines at the right edge. No pocket, no jetting, no identifiable garment part.

Clean 384x482 front-view lapel drawing (largest and clearest asset in the batch). Counted at 10x magnification: the viewer-right lapel carries exactly THREE red buttonhole dashes, the viewer-left lapel exactly TWO. In a front view the wearer's left lapel appears on the viewer's right, so this reads three buttonholes on the left lapel and two on the right - exactly the labelled 3/2 split, matching the supplier filename 'Left_three_right_two'. Both mark clusters sit on the lapel face above the notch, so the discriminator (count and side) is unambiguously drawn.

A genuine full front-view jacket line drawing (notch lapel, chest welt pocket) with the shoulders in frame, so the garment region is correct and the subject is not wrong. But the sleeve-head expression cannot be read: the caption strip at the bottom is clipped by the crop and is illegible, and stacking the shoulder band against its three siblings (regular.jpg, con-rollino.jpg, neapolitan.jpg) shows four essentially identical plain sloping shoulder lines - no roping, no shirring, no raised sleeve head. At 240x200 nothing separates 'Natural' from roped or Neapolitan, so the discriminator is not expressible.

240x200 line drawing of a jacket FRONT with both shoulder seams and sleeve-head outer seams traced in red - correct garment area for a sleeve-head option. Zoomed 22x on both shoulder points: a distinct soft gathered/puckered mass is drawn where the sleeve meets the shoulder, and the shoulder line drops steeply - a legitimate spalla camicia (shirt-shoulder) rendering, and visibly different from its sibling con-rollino.jpg (pixel diff bbox 16,4-208,200). Caption is clipped by the bottom edge of the image; only the tops of the letters survive, reading as two words beginning 'Ne...li...'. Low-resolution asset, so confidence is moderate.

Correct area (a sleeve/cuff tube with the cuff opening drawn as a swooping ellipse) but the COUNT is wrong, and count is the entire discriminator for cuff-button-number. Run-structure analysis of the red marks along the cuff vent edge gives a strict alternation of 9 solid bar bands and 8 hollow capsule bodies (bodies ~51-56px, separators ~13-23px) spanning y=350-936 - i.e. EIGHT evenly spaced marks, not four. No button discs are drawn anywhere. The marks also run far up the sleeve (starting at y=350, roughly halfway up the panel) rather than clustering at the cuff. Alternative reading: the red chain is simply a dashed highlight of the vent seam, which would say nothing about a button count either. Either way the drawing does not show 4 buttons. No caption text anywhere in the 1200x1200 frame (ink bbox x336-866, y44-1158).

Same sleeve/cuff base drawing as the '4 flat' sibling, but the red button marks near the cuff hem (y=727-960) are visibly STAGGERED and OVERLAPPING each other rather than sitting in a straight separated column - x spread 325-379 vs the flat sibling's tight 335-368, and the run structure is irregular where the flat sibling's is perfectly periodic. Side-by-side comparison makes the touching/overlapping arrangement obvious. That is exactly the kissing-vs-spaced discriminator this field is about. No caption text in frame.

Not a back view and not a vent. This is a cropped tile out of a multi-cell LAPEL / GORGE MEASUREMENT chart: jacket FRONTS on grey mannequin busts, each with a red measurement arrow across the lapel notch, and printed captions under the cells reading '5.5cm' and '6cm' (plus the red in-figure labels '5.5cm' and '6cm'). Rows of further front-view cells are cut off at the top and bottom of the crop. No jacket back, no seat, no vent of any kind appears in the image.

Same lapel-measurement chart as center-vent.jpg, a different crop. Two jacket FRONT cells with red gorge/notch measurement arrows and printed captions '4.5cm' and '5cm' (in-figure red labels '4.5cm' and '5cm'). This is a lapel-width diagram, not a back-vent diagram - there is no back view at all, so it cannot express 'no vent'.

Same lapel-measurement chart again, a third crop. Jacket FRONT cells with red measurement arrows across the lapel notch and printed captions '6.5CM' and a partially cut-off '7...' (in-figure red labels '6.5cm' and '7cm'). No back view, no side seams, no vents.

Trouser BACK view (five belt loops, centre seat seam, no fly J-stitch - confirmed by comparison with the '31A0 No' sibling which is the same base drawing). A single horizontal red BESOM welt is drawn on one side of the seat (red pixels x201-513, y275-382; zero red in the opposite half), with a small red diamond-shaped mark hanging directly below the welt = the button/buttonhole tab. Single besom + button & buttonhole on one side only is exactly what the label claims. Minor caveat: the welt sits on the image-left, which on a rear view is the wearer's right - tech packs commonly label by drawing position, so 'Left' may be drawing-relative.

Trouser BACK view, identical base drawing to the '32C7 Left besom' sibling (five belt loops, centre seat seam, back darts) but with the seat completely clean - zero red pixels in the whole file and no welt, no jetting, no button. Because the sibling image places a pocket in exactly this area, the empty seat reads unambiguously as 'no back pockets'.

Waistband EXTENSION construction detail: waistband curtain (zigzag top edge), fly/zip area, and the extension tab outlined in red with a pointed V end, dimensioned by a red caption reading exactly '13cm'. The red tab is visibly the longest of the set, consistent with the largest value. (Unrelated boxed annotation in the drawing reads '洗水唛' = wash-care label placement.)
Same waistband-extension detail drawing; red extension tab is the longest in the whole family and the red dimension caption reads exactly '15cm'.
Waistband-extension detail with the red-outlined extension tab and a red dimension caption reading exactly '5cm'; tab is the shortest of the set.
Waistband-extension detail; red dimension caption reads '5. 5cm' (space is a rendering artefact of the source drawing), matching the 5.5 cm label. Tab length sits between the 5cm and 6cm siblings.
Waistband-extension detail; red dimension caption reads exactly '6cm', and the red extension tab is proportionally longer than the 5.5cm sibling.
Waistband-extension detail; red dimension caption reads exactly '6.5cm'.
Waistband-extension detail; red dimension caption reads exactly '7cm'.

Wrong garment part. The drawing is a trouser FRONT, but the red topstitch highlight is entirely on the two slant SIDE-POCKET openings, not on the fly: red pixels occupy x61-1125 with EXACTLY ZERO red pixels in the centre third (x450-750) where the fly sits. A 3x zoom of the left hip shows the red line running parallel and just inside a black diagonal that descends from the waistband to the hip and terminates in a bar-tack tick - a classic quarter-top/slant pocket mouth. The centre-front fly J-stitch is drawn as a plain unhighlighted black line, identical to its 'no topstitch' sibling, which proves the option family is not about the fly. Nothing curved-vs-straight about a fly is expressed.

A real, correct trouser FRONT drawing that does include the fly, and it contains zero red pixels - so 'no topstitching' is depicted by absence, which is defensible. But it cannot express that the absent stitching is on the FLY: it is the same base drawing as its two siblings (31A1/31A3), and in those siblings the red topstitch is applied to the slant side-pocket mouths, never to the fly. The fly J-curve is rendered identically as a bare black line in all three files, so a viewer has nothing here that reads as a fly-topstitch option.

Same problem as its 0.6cm sibling: trouser FRONT with the red topstitch highlight on the two slant SIDE-POCKET openings only - red pixels x84-1120 with ZERO red in the centre third (x450-750) where the fly is. The fly J-stitch is plain black and unhighlighted. The file is a genuinely different image from the 0.6cm sibling (11,614 vs 17,431 red pixels, i.e. a thinner stitch offset matching 0.15cm vs 0.6cm), but the feature being dimensioned is pocket topstitching, not fly topstitching.

Trouser FRONT with exactly four red pleat strokes measured in the pleat band - two on the left (x369-398, x439-454) and two on the right (x723-737, x780-809) - i.e. DOUBLE pleats on each side, plainly legible. A red magnifier-circle callout at top-left enlarges the pleat fold in cross-section to indicate fold direction (toward the fly). The count discriminator is unmistakable; the forward-vs-reverse direction rests on the small inset, which is legible but modest.

Effectively a blank asset. The entire 1200x1200 file contains nothing but one long thin horizontal band (ink bbox x42-1149, y515-669): a black-outlined rectangle with a solid red stripe running edge to edge through the middle (red pixels y556-610). There is no waistband, no curtain, no piping edge, no Snugtex gripper texture, no seam, no scale, no callout and no caption - verified at 8x vertical zoom, the red stripe is a flat solid fill with no internal detail. It cannot depict any of the three things the label names.

Correct area: a 240x200 jacket FRONT with the shoulder seam and sleeve-head outer seam traced in red, and it is a genuinely distinct drawing from neapolitan.jpg. But at 20-22x zoom on both shoulder points the sleeve/shoulder junction is just a clean sharp angle with a straighter, slightly more extended shoulder line - no rollino roping, no raised sleeve-head roll is rendered, so the actual con-rollino construction cannot be read. Caption is clipped off by the bottom edge of the image; only the tops of four word-groups survive, consistent with 'Con rollino sho...' but not legible enough to quote. Too small and too under-drawn to confirm the discriminator.

Jacket front line drawing cropped to the shoulders and sleeve heads. The shoulder line runs nearly flat out from the neck and breaks at a defined shoulder point before the sleeve drops - the built-up, squared structured/English shoulder. Partial caption is visible below the drawing, cut off mid-height, beginning with 'R' (cropped 'Regular'). Not a subject error but a quality defect: this file is a UI screenshot, carrying a baked-in navy card selection border and a blue selection checkmark in the lower-right corner, with the caption sliced off at the bottom edge.

Same jacket-front view as its sibling, but the shoulder line slopes downward continuously and more steeply from neck into sleeve with no built-up shoulder point - the soft, unstructured shirt-style sleeve head. Cropped caption below the drawing reads 'Shirt Head'. Confirmed a genuinely different drawing from regular.jpg (different md5; shoulder geometry visibly differs side by side), though the difference is subtle at 240x200.

Trouser hip blueprint. The red highlight traces a pocket mouth that drops vertically from the waistband seam then turns at a clean right angle and runs across to the seam - the square-cornered western/jeans pocket opening. The right-angle corner is precisely what 'square' distinguishes (versus a curved scoop). The back besom pocket is drawn separately in black on the right and is left unhighlighted, so there is no confusion about which pocket is being specified.

Same trouser hip blueprint family. The red highlight is a single long, straight, clean vertical slit on the front panel, running parallel to and just forward of the seam, with no flap, no curve and no corner - a jetted/besom slot pocket. Measured at roughly 470px of a 1200px frame against a ~95px waistband, which scales to a plausible ~20cm jetted opening. Filename also carries the factory's own '__Besom' tag.

Trouser front, fly area. The base drawing shows the waistband extension tab overlapping past the fly with a buttonhole in it (small dark oval), the fly topstitch line running down, and the curved fly-J seam below. The red hand-drawn hook mark sits exactly at the junction of the waistband extension and the top of the fly - the French fly extension/hook closure, which is the defining feature of the option. The red annotation is small and crudely drawn (reads like a bracket), but it is correctly placed.

Side view of trousers with the leg bottom shown enlarged. A red line runs straight across the leg roughly 87px above the leg opening, with plain uninterrupted fabric below it and no fold or turn-up band - a plain hem with the hem allowance depth marked. Row-darkness scan of the hem zone finds only two horizontal features: the red depth line (rows 1054-1073) and the leg-opening edge (rows 1137-1160). The literal 7.6 cm value is not readable from the drawing, but the 'plain' variant is correctly and unambiguously shown.

No cuff or turn-up is drawn anywhere in this image. The leg bottom is identical to the 'Plain Hem' blueprint (87f09a00ddf2__3609.jpg): a row-darkness scan across the leg interior in the hem zone finds only the faint pink highlight band (rows 1091-1099) and the same leg-opening edge (rows 1137-1160, byte-for-byte the same rows as the plain-hem file). There is no second horizontal line, no fold line, and no doubled band, and the trouser crease line runs uninterrupted straight through to the bottom edge - all of which a turn-up would break. The only difference from the plain-hem drawing is that the highlight sits lower on the leg. It therefore depicts a plain hem at a shallower depth, not a 3.8 cm cuff turn-up. The highlight is also washed out to pale pink (only 118 saturated red pixels versus 4475 in the plain-hem file), making it barely visible.

Shirt collar front view. Red 45-degree diagonal hatching - the standard bias-grain convention - fills exactly the visible triangular front of the collar band beneath the collar points, the panel containing the collar button. That triangle is the outer collar stand as seen from outside the garment. Cross-checked against the sibling bias_cutting/inner-collar-stand.jpg, which hatches the inside band at the back of the neck instead, confirming the outer/inner discriminator is genuinely expressed by which region is hatched.

Shirt front with red button marks down the placket, counted programmatically. One red mark sits at the collar band (the collar button, which the option explicitly excludes) plus exactly 6 marks below it, at rows 42, 64, 86, 109, 131 and 153. Two sub-pixel red specks (3px and 1px) are JPEG artifacts, not buttons. Count is exact and the spacing is the widest of the four-image set, consistent with the lowest button count.

Same shirt-front drawing. One red collar-band mark (excluded per the label) plus exactly 7 red button marks below it, at rows 32, 51, 72, 92, 113, 133 and 154. Count is exact and spacing tightens correctly relative to the 6-button image.
Same shirt-front drawing. One red collar-band mark (excluded per the label) plus exactly 8 red button marks below it, at rows 32, 48, 66, 84, 101, 118, 137 and 154. Count is exact.

Same shirt-front drawing. One red collar-band mark (excluded per the label) plus exactly 9 red button marks below it, at rows 31, 47, 61, 77, 93, 109, 124, 140 and 156. Count is exact and spacing is the tightest of the set, consistent with the highest button count.

The drawing is of the right area - a shirt front with red vertical buttonholes marked down the placket - but at 178x267 px the hand-versus-machine distinction is a stitch-character difference that simply cannot be rendered. Decisively, this file is byte-identical to buttonhole/machine.jpg (both 7812 bytes, both md5 568e2a13d9caf35fda8461fbfb0c5dc3), so the exact same picture is serving both options and cannot discriminate between them by construction. Needs a real macro photograph of hand-worked versus machine-worked buttonholes, not a line drawing.

Identical situation to its sibling: byte-identical file to buttonhole/hand-made.jpg (same 7812 bytes, same md5 568e2a13d9caf35fda8461fbfb0c5dc3). It is a correct drawing of placket buttonholes but expresses nothing about machine versus hand construction, and cannot, since one file serves both options.

Both halves of the claim verified. Six buttonholes run down the placket at rows 42, 63, 83, 105, 127 and 147. A magnifier balloon's pointer tail lands on the buttonhole at row 127 - counting up from the bottom (147 is 1st), that is exactly the 2nd from the bottom. Inside the balloon, the enlarged buttonhole is drawn as a red HORIZONTAL dash across the placket, while the buttonholes on the placket itself are short vertical ticks. The balloon body also happens to sit over the row-105 buttonhole, but the tail unambiguously points at row 127.

The cleanest and largest drawing in this batch (574x802). Every buttonhole down the placket is drawn as a distinct vertical slot with its button, and a blue magnifier balloon points at the lowest buttonhole and enlarges it to show a red HORIZONTAL buttonhole. That is precisely 'vertical buttonholes with one horizontal buttonhole', with both states visible in the same frame for direct comparison.

Sleeve shown with a turned-up/rolled hem (fold lines visible). A narrow strap with a pointed end and a button, sitting at the sleeve hem, is filled solid red - the cuff/sleeve tab. Solid-red fill is this folder's consistent convention for 'apply the contrast colour to this piece' (confirmed against contrast_color_position/outer-cuff.jpg, where the whole barrel cuff is filled red), so the fill correctly identifies which component takes the contrast fabric.

Close angled view of the neck and shoulder: the collar leaf, the collar band with its buttonhole at the rounded front end, and the front placket with its buttonhole are all identifiable, with the sleeve-head arc below. The strap running from the sleeve head up toward the collar, with a pointed free end and a button, is filled solid red - the shoulder epaulet, correctly located on the shoulder rather than on a sleeve or cuff.

Long sleeve terminating in a barrel cuff with its button and topstitching. The narrow gauntlet/tower placket running up the sleeve from the cuff, with its gabled pointed top and gauntlet button, is filled solid red - the sleeve vent placket. Distinct drawing and distinct garment area from the cuff-tab and shoulder-epaulet entries, so the field's positions are genuinely differentiated.

Same base drawing as contrast_color_position/shoulder-epaulet.jpg but with the strap outlined in red rather than filled, which is the correct convention for a shape option instead of a colour option. The strap is sewn in at the sleeve head and runs up toward the collar, and its free end is clearly gabled/POINTED with a button at the point, plus dashed edge stitching down both sides - a pointed shoulder epaulet. The folder's only other option is none.jpg, so pointed is the sole shape offered and the drawing shows it.

Full shirt front with a small label/tag drawn at the bottom of the front placket just above the hem; the position is marked in red with the letter 'A' plus a stroke over the tag. The position discriminator is genuinely expressed - sibling picture-1114.jpg marks 'B' higher up at the second-lowest button and picture-1115.jpg marks 'C' at the collar, so the three occupy visibly different spots. Caveat for the caller: the image's own caption is 'A', not '2'. Per data-store/options/shirt.json the 'Position N' names are auto-generated sequence labels (blp-1..blp-5), and the numbering is offset because blp-1 'Position 1' maps to picture-1112.jpg, which is not a shirt at all but a Chinese text card reading 'No Button', while blp-5 'Position 5' maps to picture-1116.jpg, which is a blank image. Those two blueprints are outside this batch but are worth flagging as broken.

Shirt front technical flat with a red position marker 'B' and a leader line pointing to the bottom of the front placket at the side-vent split. It is a genuine brand-label position diagram and marks one specific spot. Sibling images confirm the scheme is offset by one: blp-2 'Position 2' = picture-1113 marked 'A' (bottom placket, slightly lower/left), blp-4 'Position 4' = picture-1115 marked 'C' (inside back neck), so Position 3 = 'B' is internally consistent.

180x180 flat/opened-out drawing of the collar and its band viewed from the underside (buttonhole at the left band end, button at the right band end).
